page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and multi-core performance in the top 25%. The PassMark CPU score of 51,157.15 and encryption test score of 39,771.17 also rank in the top 25%. Memory performance is solid, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25%, though memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes fall within the middle 50% average. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, achieving 339.19 tokens per second, while prompt processing and medium-sized model inference speeds remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation combined with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a dense compute profile suitable for CPU-bound tasks without the overhead of unneeded memory. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage adds value for disk-I/O intensive operations. This hardware configuration is well-suited for workloads such as multi-threaded compilation, data compression, encryption tasks, web serving, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% and 25% respectively. This configuration is highly suitable for compute-intensive workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and data compression tasks requiring dedicated CPU resources without excessive memory overhead.
